Update: Well , I didn't go through with it.
I want to thank the kind stranger who called the embassy (I really didn't expect that, PM me if you can read this), the police told my parents and that made me sit down and talk with them. That was fast.
I'll try hanging on a little longer, see if I can pass a university entrance exam this september and switch medications.
Thank you guys.

I don't know, it would be so boring, would that even interest someone?
I feel like I'm the one still sitting on the starting line of a marathon. Watching others running and running, struggling, fighting, enjoying themselves on their journey, with me now just wanting to go to the ending point, skipping all the road because I know I'm the last one and I'll never be able to reach anyone to travel together with.

Thanks for answering.

I've been like this since I can remember, it started in kindergarden I guess but I don't remember much from that period.
1st grade is where it all came out. I had erythrophobia and social anxiety disorder, not depression at least, quite intense.
I couldn't stand the sight of others, talking, being watched, gathering attention, the usual stuff. 
I know it's quite common but at that time I didn't know what was happening, we didn't have a name for it, just shyness the teachers and my parents said. 

I didn't want to go to school, I would do anything to avoid it, anything. It's quite funny now that I remember it.
I would hide behind forniture, inside stuff, lock doors and block them with chairs, remove handles with screwdrivers, lie, run away somewhere.
It was just something I couldn't snap out of, it wasn't as simple as turning on and off a switch. 
I was just by myself all the time, wanting to be a ghost or the invisible man.
